---
title: ""
# pagetitle: "Srivatsan Balaji"
---

<canvas id="cube-bg"></canvas>
<div id="cube-veil"></div>

<style>
/* base colour lives on <html> so nothing else needs to paint a background */
html { background: #05070e; }

/* static stand-in for the wave-grid when WebGL isn't available — echoes the
   neon palette (colorA/colorB in the script below) without any animation */
html.no-webgl {
  background:
    radial-gradient(ellipse 120% 70% at 50% 10%, rgba(205,44,119,0.24), transparent 60%),
    radial-gradient(ellipse 120% 70% at 50% 95%, rgba(44,162,205,0.20), transparent 60%),
    #05070e;
}

/* let the animation show through every Quarto wrapper, navbar included */
body,
header#quarto-header,
#quarto-header .navbar,
#quarto-content,
#quarto-document-content,
.quarto-container,
.page-columns,
main.content,
.navbar-container,
.quarto-title-block {
  background: transparent !important;
}

#cube-bg {
  position: fixed;
  inset: 0;
  width: 100vw; height: 100vh;
  z-index: -2;
  pointer-events: none;
  opacity: 0.30;          /* dial down so body copy stays readable */
}

/* scrim between the animation and the text — raise the alpha if body copy
   still competes with the brighter parts of the wave */
#cube-veil {
  position: fixed;
  inset: 0;
  width: 100vw; height: 100vh;
  z-index: -1;
  pointer-events: none;
  background: radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 40%,
              rgba(5,7,14,0.55) 0%, rgba(5,7,14,0.80) 100%);
}

/* keep the nav readable now that it sits on moving cubes */
#quarto-header .navbar {
  backdrop-filter: blur(0px);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
  box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
}
</style>

<script>
(function () {
  const canvas = document.getElementById('cube-bg');
  const veil   = document.getElementById('cube-veil');
  if (!canvas) return;

  /* Quarto renders this markup inside its content column, and any ancestor with
     a transform/filter would become the containing block for a fixed element —
     which is what boxes the canvas into the column. Reparenting to <body>
     guarantees it is positioned against the viewport instead. This is plain DOM
     work, independent of WebGL/Three.js, so it happens even on the fallback path. */
  document.body.appendChild(canvas);
  if (veil) document.body.appendChild(veil);

  function supportsWebGL() {
    try {
      const test = document.createElement('canvas');
      return !!(window.WebGLRenderingContext &&
        (test.getContext('webgl') || test.getContext('experimental-webgl')));
    } catch (e) {
      return false;
    }
  }

  if (!supportsWebGL()) {
    document.documentElement.classList.add('no-webgl');   // static gradient (see <style>) carries the page
    return;
  }

  import('https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/0.185.1/three.module.min.js')
    .then((THREE) => run(THREE))
    .catch(() => document.documentElement.classList.add('no-webgl'));

  function run(THREE) {
  THREE.ColorManagement.enabled = false;   // r128 parity: use hex colours as raw values, no sRGB reinterpretation

  // fewer cells and a lower pixel-ratio cap on small/handheld viewports — the
  // per-frame grid update is O(density^2), so this is where the cost lives
  const smallViewport = Math.min(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight) <= 760;

  const CFG = {
    density  : smallViewport ? 96 : 160,       // cubes per side
    amplitude: 0.80,     // wave height, in spacings
    speed    : 0.50,
    glow     : 3.00,
    tilt     : 90,       // camera elevation, degrees
    colorA   : '#cd2c77',
    colorB   : '#2ca2cd',
    fog      : 0x0a1420,

    /* --- unit-cell deformation --------------------------------------------
       shear tips each cell to follow the local surface slope.
       strain scales axial deformation with local curvature (tension at
       crests, compression in troughs); poisson is the transverse response,
       negative being auxetic. Both are inert while strain is 0.            */
    strain   : 0.00,     // 0 = cells stay rigid, only tipping
    poisson  : -0.40,
    shear    : 2.00
  };

  const CAM_DIST  = 20;    // camera distance; screen coverage comes from spacing
  const FILL      = 0.95;  // cube size as a fraction of spacing
  const TOP_REACH = 4.0;   // ground distance at top of frame, in camera heights

  const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas, antialias: true, alpha: true });
  renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, smallViewport ? 1.5 : 2));
  renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0);

  const scene = new THREE.Scene();
  scene.fog = new THREE.FogExp2(CFG.fog, 0.02);
  const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(45, 1, 0.1, 400);

  const uniforms = {
    uGlow  : { value: CFG.glow },
    uColorA: { value: new THREE.Color(CFG.colorA) },
    uColorB: { value: new THREE.Color(CFG.colorB) },
    uMaxH  : { value: 1.0 }
  };

  // neon lives on the cube edges: distance to the nearest face border in UV space
  const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
    uniforms,
    vertexShader: `
      varying vec2 vUv;
      varying float vFace;
      varying float vH;
      void main(){
        vUv   = uv;
        vFace = abs(normal.y);
        vec4 ip = instanceMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
        vH = ip.y;
        gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * ip;
      }
    `,
    fragmentShader: `
      uniform float uGlow;
      uniform vec3  uColorA;
      uniform vec3  uColorB;
      uniform float uMaxH;
      varying vec2  vUv;
      varying float vFace;
      varying float vH;

      void main(){
        vec2 d = min(vUv, 1.0 - vUv);
        float edge = min(d.x, d.y);

        float core = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.030, edge);   // crisp filament
        float halo = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.170, edge);   // soft bleed
        float line = core + halo * 0.42;

        float t = clamp(vH / (uMaxH * 2.0) + 0.5, 0.0, 1.0);
        vec3 neon = mix(uColorB, uColorA, t);

        vec3 faceCol = vec3(0.030, 0.042, 0.075) * (0.55 + vFace * 0.55);
        float lift = 0.55 + t * 0.9;                       // peaks glow brighter

        gl_FragColor = vec4(faceCol + neon * line * uGlow * lift, 1.0);
      }
    `
  });

  const N = CFG.density;
  const dummy = new THREE.Object3D();
  let SPACING = 1.0;

  const mesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1), material, N * N);
  mesh.instanceMatrix.setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage);
  mesh.frustumCulled = false;
  scene.add(mesh);

  // The camera sits at CFG.tilt but aims lower, so the top of the frame lands on
  // ground TOP_REACH camera-heights out. The horizon is never in shot, so there
  // is no empty background above the field.
  function fitField() {
    const fovY  = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(camera.fov);
    const fovX  = 2 * Math.atan(Math.tan(fovY / 2) * camera.aspect);
    const pitch = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(CFG.tilt);

    const height = Math.sin(pitch) * CAM_DIST;
    const horiz  = Math.cos(pitch) * CAM_DIST;

    const topAngle  = Math.atan(1 / TOP_REACH);
    const viewPitch = topAngle + fovY / 2;
    const farDist   = height * TOP_REACH;
    const aimZ      = horiz - height / Math.tan(viewPitch);

    // stretch the grid until it reaches every corner of the frustum
    const R = Math.max(horiz + farDist, farDist * Math.tan(fovX / 2)) * 1.15 + 4;
    SPACING = (2 * R) / N;
    scene.fog.density = 0.90 / R;

    camera.position.set(0, height, horiz);
    camera.lookAt(0, 0, aimZ);
  }

  // height field, filled once per frame and then differenced for strain
  const HS = new Float32Array(N * N);

  function waveAt(gx, gz) {
    const gr = Math.sqrt(gx * gx + gz * gz);
    return Math.sin(gx * 0.32 + TIME * 1.1)  * 0.55 +
           Math.cos(gz * 0.28 - TIME * 0.85) * 0.55 +
           Math.sin(gr * 0.42 - TIME * 1.4)  * 0.45;
  }

  let TIME = 0;

  function updateGrid(t) {
    TIME = t;
    const half = (N - 1) / 2;
    const s    = SPACING * FILL;
    const amp  = CFG.amplitude * SPACING;

    // pass 1 — sample the height field
    for (let x = 0; x < N; x++) {
      for (let z = 0; z < N; z++) {
        HS[x * N + z] = waveAt(x - half, z - half);
      }
    }

    // pass 2 — differentiate it, then place and deform each cell
    const at = (x, z) => HS[Math.min(N-1, Math.max(0, x)) * N +
                            Math.min(N-1, Math.max(0, z))];

    // slope in world terms: amp per grid step, so SPACING cancels out
    const slopeGain = CFG.amplitude * CFG.shear;
    let i = 0;

    for (let x = 0; x < N; x++) {
      for (let z = 0; z < N; z++) {
        const h  = HS[x * N + z];

        // central differences: slope drives shear, curvature drives strain
        const dx  = (at(x+1, z) - at(x-1, z)) * 0.5;
        const dz  = (at(x, z+1) - at(x, z-1)) * 0.5;
        const lap = at(x+1, z) + at(x-1, z) + at(x, z+1) + at(x, z-1) - 4 * h;

        // negative curvature (a crest) puts the cell in tension
        let eps = -lap * CFG.strain;
        eps = Math.max(-0.55, Math.min(0.55, eps));

        const sy  = s * (1 + eps);
        const sxz = s * (1 - CFG.poisson * eps);   // transverse response

        dummy.position.set((x - half) * SPACING, h * amp, (z - half) * SPACING);
        dummy.scale.set(sxz, sy, sxz);
        dummy.rotation.set(-dz * slopeGain, 0, dx * slopeGain);
        dummy.updateMatrix();
        mesh.setMatrixAt(i++, dummy.matrix);
      }
    }
    mesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true;
    uniforms.uMaxH.value = amp;
  }

  function resize() {
    const w = window.innerWidth, h = window.innerHeight;
    renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
    camera.aspect = w / h;
    camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
    fitField();
  }
  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);
  resize();

  const clock = new THREE.Clock();
  let time = 0, running = false;

  function frame() {
    if (document.hidden) { running = false; return; }   // pause in background tabs
    running = true;
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
    time += clock.getDelta() * CFG.speed;
    updateGrid(time);
    renderer.render(scene, camera);
  }

  function start() {
    if (running) return;
    clock.getDelta();                                    // drop time spent paused
    frame();
  }

  if (window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
    updateGrid(0);                                       // single static frame
    renderer.render(scene, camera);
  } else {
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (!document.hidden) start(); });
    start();
  }
  }
})();
</script>

::: {.message style="max-width: 1100px; margin: 60px auto 0; line-height: 1.6;"}

::: {.text-center}

#### Designing adaptive robotic hardware that help robots work reliably in the messy real world.
:::

::: {style="text-align: justify; margin-top: 30px;"}
My goal is to enhance the capabilities of robots by building hardware that overcomes existing physical limitations. By integrating compliant mechanisms, designing torsion-resistant metamaterials, and embedding flexible tactile sensors. When the hardware is smart, adaptive, and structurally resilient, the software boundary expands.
:::
